Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

stanimal (development version)

  • The worked examples are now vignettes (browseVignettes("stanimal")), and the package has a website with the reference and the vignettes as articles, https://diogro.github.io/stanimal/. The vignettes are precomputed, so building or checking the package does not fit any model. The scripts they replace are gone from examples/, which keeps the long simulation studies and cross-package comparisons.

stanimal 0.9.0

  • lmm_animal() and lmm_animal_laplace() gain correlation_prior. The default "lkj" is the existing prior. "size" writes each correlation matrix of an unstructured G and E as one dense size factor plus an LKJ remainder, D (l l' + R) D, with loadings pooled around a mean loading the data estimate, so that traits sharing a size axis are no longer all shrunk toward zero correlation. In simulations of size-dominated traits the LKJ fits recovered about half the true genetic correlations and heritabilities, and the size prior recovered them with nominal coverage, matching or beating fits to size_shape() scores. "shared_size" also gives G and E one standardized loading pattern. Both use parametrization = "h2" and report rho_G, rho_E, sigma_size_G, sigma_size_E, size_loadings_G, size_loadings_E, integration_G and integration_E. Fits record correlation_prior.
  • animal_prior_draws() gains correlation_prior, and plot_prior_posterior() and plot_forest() rebuild the size prior from the recorded configuration. Older fits without the attribute are read as LKJ fits.

stanimal 0.8.3

  • fit_loo() gains transform, which moves the terms of a fit to size_shape() scores onto the original traits, so loo_compare() can set a size-shape fit against a fit to the raw traits. The scores are one linear map of every individual’s traits, so the change is a single constant per term (the Jacobian of the map and the change of standardization), exact for a complete response with every shape axis kept. Responses completed before the rotation, fewer shape axes, and a transform whose scores are not the fit’s response are refused. The result carries attr(, "scale") = "traits".

stanimal 0.8.2

  • fit_loo() now leaves out one individual at a time for animal fits, and works with missing trait records. Relatives share breeding values, so the animal model does not factorize over individuals; each term is the conditional density of an animal’s observed traits given every other animal, computed after the fit from the draws of G, E, beta and Y_mis (the non-factorized LOO of Bürkner, Gabry & Vehtari 2021). An animal’s own gaps are integrated out and the others’ are conditioned on at their sampled values, which keeps the importance sampling exact. Before, the terms were records rotated by the eigenvectors of A, which are not animals, and fits with gaps were refused. That criterion remains as unit = "record" (complete responses only). ELPD values from earlier versions are not comparable with the new default. eigen_A skips the decomposition of A, and attr(, "units") names the animal of each term. Custom model_file fits need unit = "record".

  • opossum_grm is now VanRaden’s genomic relationship matrix, Z Z' / (2 sum p (1 - p)), the same matrix genomic_relationship() returns for these markers. It was Z Z' / m, 2.86 times smaller, with a diagonal near 0.37 instead of about 1, so a G fitted on it was the covariance for a relationship no animal had: G and the heritabilities came out inflated. Fits on the old matrix are not comparable with fits on the new one; genetic correlations depend on the scale only through the prior, so they change little.

  • Chains start from init = 1, a draw on (-1, 1) on the unconstrained scale, instead of the engines’ (-2, 2). The chains still start apart, so Rhat can detect a mode that only some visit, but a correlation factor over many traits no longer starts nearly singular. With 35 traits the wider start stalled every chain (step size ~1e-21, 27% divergent transitions) in 5 of 5 seeds; init = 1 and init = 0.5 started all of them cleanly. Pass init through ... to override.

  • The unstructured lm_phen_cov() model no longer multiplies out its Cholesky factor and factorizes the product again for each pattern of observed traits. A pattern that observes every trait uses the factor directly; an incomplete one takes it from a QR decomposition of the factor’s rows. Refactorizing failed in floating point when the factor had tiny diagonal entries, so a 35-trait fit could reject every initial value. This regressed in 0.8.0 with incomplete trait records, and complete-data fits also save one K x K Cholesky per gradient.

  • The default adapt_delta drops from 0.99 to 0.9 for lm_phen_cov() and for lmm_animal(genetic_structure = "factor") with an unstructured or diagonal residual. Those fits run 2 to 3 times faster in the examples with no divergences. Univariate, unstructured-G and shared-factor fits keep 0.99: at 0.9 the unstructured model diverged in about half of the power-simulation fits at 48 or 96 animals, and the shared-factor test fit in 6 of 10 seeds. lmm_animal()’s control now defaults to NULL, which picks the target from the structure. Pass control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99) for the old behaviour everywhere.

  • Laplace fits (lmm_animal_laplace(), lm_phen_cov_laplace()) label their summary and draws with the column names of Y and X (G[wing,tail], h2[tail], beta[tail,size]), as fit_draws() names sampler fits, and record them as y_names and x_names. An unnamed Y keeps Stan’s indices. Code that looked quantities up as G[1,1] on a named Y must use the names.

stanimal 0.8.1

Bug fixes

  • Two fits of the same model in one session that started from the same random state within a minute (for example with set.seed() before each fit) wrote to the same CmdStan output files. The first fit then silently returned the second fit’s draws, and garbage-collecting the first fit deleted the second’s files. cmdstanr builds output names from the minute, the process id and one runif(); stanimal now gives every sampler run a unique output_basename (from tempfile(), which set.seed() does not affect). Laplace fits read their draws at once and keep no fit, so they were not affected. An output_dir or output_basename passed through ... is respected.

stanimal 0.8.0

New features

  • lmm_animal() gains eigen_A, a precomputed eigendecomposition of A (list(Q =, lambda =), e.g. from eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE)). A caller fitting many models on the same relationship matrix, such as one model per trait subset, pays the O(N^3) decomposition once instead of once per fit. It works with every structure and parametrization, is checked against A (reconstruction and orthonormality) before fitting, follows A when it is reordered to match Y, and takes blend_A. The decomposition can come from any solver, including a GPU one.

Changes in behaviour

  • The animal models take the eigendecomposition of A as data instead of decomposing A themselves in Stan. lmm_animal() and lmm_animal_laplace() decompose it once per fit in R; previously every chain repeated it, computing the eigenvectors and the eigenvalues separately. The model is unchanged: the eigenvalues are passed in Stan’s ascending order, and in the tests a model that decomposes A the old way reproduces the new one draw for draw. Where A has repeated eigenvalues the two libraries may choose different bases for them, which can change the MCMC trajectory through rounding but not the posterior. A custom model_file that declares A still receives it.
  • The decomposition now runs on R’s BLAS/LAPACK. With an optimised library (OpenBLAS, MKL, Accelerate) it is several times faster than Stan’s; with R’s reference LAPACK it is about 1.5 times slower, so a single large fit can take slightly longer in wall clock (about 6% at N = 4000) while using a third of the CPU. Use an optimised BLAS for large N, or pass eigen_A.
  • fit_loo() and the loo() fit methods now refuse LOO and WAIC for animal fits with missing responses; fits without response metadata warn that their likelihood terms cannot be verified.
  • plot_G_ellipses() now labels each trait pair with its own genetic correlation and interval when there are four or more traits.

Bug fixes

  • Animal posterior predictive replicates now use the correct relationship covariance between individuals.
  • breeding_values() retains imputation-based predictions but now computes standard errors and reliabilities conditional only on observed responses.
  • Univariate breeding values use the posterior mean variances, not squared posterior mean standard deviations.
  • Predictive summaries now use the same observed-entry masks as the data.
  • size_shape() now reports an actionable error when the requested shape axes exceed the numerical rank of the centered shape data.
  • genomic_relationship() excludes fully missing markers even with supplied frequencies and max_missing = 1, warning when they would otherwise pass the filters.
  • Relabeling fit_draws now also updates the trait labels of factor loadings.
  • Missing-data EM starts with a positive-definite covariance and errors on non-convergence or singularity; design diagnostics warn if unavailable.

Documentation

  • Corrected the opossum data help and example and agent guides.
  • Corrected LKJ-use warnings, prior and model-comparison guidance, and posterior predictive tail-probability explanations.

stanimal 0.7.4

Bug fixes

  • breeding_values() now computes reliability using the individual’s prior variance, A[n,n] * G[k,k], instead of assuming unit diagonals in A.

  • Laplace fits write the optimization mode at high precision, avoiding a Cholesky round-trip failure caused by insufficient CSV precision. They no longer suppress warnings or retry unrelated errors; a failed Laplace stage reports CmdStan output. Explicitly supplied unused model arguments warn as in the samplers.

Changes in behaviour

  • plot_prior_posterior() and plot_forest() can now reconstruct the ordinary factor-G prior by simulating its recorded horseshoe and factor settings. Shared-factor fits still require explicitly supplied prior draws.

  • plot_prior_posterior() and plot_forest() now require explicit prior draws for bare draws or fits missing the metadata needed to reconstruct the prior, rather than silently assuming the default model. They validate supplied prior labels and use recorded trait names, and warn when an LKJ override differs from the fitted prior.

Documentation and tests

  • Added a runnable Laplace example and tests covering model configurations, missing responses, error reporting, and a comparison with sampling.
  • Clarified prior, breeding-value and data documentation. Removed committed build and check artifacts and updated the development workflow to keep them outside the checkout.

stanimal 0.7.3

Documentation

  • ratones_morpho and ratones_pedigree stay, with a weak identification section explaining what they are: a long-term artificial-selection experiment that happens to carry a pedigree, in which 329 individuals from 58 sires identify a 35-trait G only weakly, so a heritability read from lmm_animal() on these traits depends on the prior as much as on the data. They remain the small worked example; opossum and opossum_grm are the datasets for anything about genetic covariance.

New data

  • opossum and opossum_grm ship with the package: 553 Monodelphis domestica from Porto et al. (2016), measured on the same 35 cranial landmarks as ratones_morpho, together with a genomic relationship matrix built from their 3,696 markers. The data are stored untransformed, as the published analysis used them. The genomic matrix is the right relationship matrix for these animals: the colony pedigree shipped with the archive puts every pair at a kinship of 0.69 to 0.93, which leaves additive variance indistinguishable from a shared colony effect.

Changes in behaviour

  • hs_slab_scale now defaults to 1 instead of 2. The earlier explanation that the slab alone determines expected communality was incorrect: the entire horseshoe prior, factor count and decay determine its distribution. With 600 individuals and 12 traits the factor model recovers a simulated G to a relative MSE of 0.07 at a slab of 2, while on the mice data the slab moved the posterior mean heritability through 0.10, 0.21, 0.78 and 0.80 at slabs of 0.5, 1, 2 and 4. A factor fit is therefore reproducible only if the slab is reported with it, and hs_slab_scale should be reported alongside the other factor prior settings. hs_global_scale is left at 1; across 0.1 to 4 the same mouse fit moved its heritability between 0.785 and 0.790, a result specific to that example.

stanimal 0.7.2

New features

  • parametrization = "h2" now applies to the unstructured multivariate model as well as to the univariate ones. It writes the two scales as a phenotypic scale and a heritability per trait, s_G = sqrt(h2) s_P and s_E = sqrt(1-h2) s_P, and puts beta_prior on the trait heritabilities. The default is unchanged ("variance"), and the two parameterizations agree when the data are informative, so this is the switch to reach for when there are few individuals per trait or when the heritability itself is the object of inference.

Bug fixes

  • The ordinary factor model now puts the beta prior on the trait heritabilities instead of on two standard deviations. The response is standardized trait by trait, so s_G^2 + s_E^2 is the phenotypic variance and the data pin it near 1, which made the old half-normal priors on s_G and s_E a prior on a circle: the density induced on h2 was Beta(1/2, 1/2), with about 14% of its mass below 0.05 and 14% above 0.95 and a moderate heritability the least likely answer a priori. At a few hundred individuals the likelihood is weak enough for that to show through, and a fit could sit at either end of the range, reporting h2 near 0 or near 1 with genetic correlations to match. The model is now parameterized by a phenotypic scale s_P and a heritability h2, with s_G = sqrt(h2) s_P and s_E = sqrt(1 - h2) s_P, so beta_prior (default c(1, 1), flat on h2) is the prior on the trait heritabilities and s_P is the free scale. h2 is still reported and still equals diag(G) / diag(P). The fits record parametrization = "h2", and s_P is a reported parameter.

stanimal 0.7.1

New features

  • lmm_animal_laplace() and lm_phen_cov_laplace() fit the same models by a Laplace approximation at the posterior mode instead of sampling them. They return posterior means and standard deviations for the covariance quantities and finish in a fraction of the time, and they deliberately return no draws: there are no chains, so there are no convergence diagnostics, and the draw-based functions refuse the result. The standard deviation of a variance or a heritability is the least reliable number they report, because a Gaussian at the mode misstates a skewed posterior.

stanimal 0.7.0

New features

  • Incomplete trait records are used instead of discarded. Y may contain NA in lmm_animal() and lm_phen_cov(): a record is kept as long as it has one observed trait, and the missing values no longer require dropping the row and losing the traits that were measured. lm_phen_cov() evaluates each missingness pattern on its observed subvector of P, so the gaps are integrated out and cost no parameters; lmm_animal() fills them with parameters (Y_mis, reported in the draws), which is the exact marginal over the observed data and lets relatives inform a gap. A fully missing record is allowed in the animal model and an error elsewhere.
  • animal_design() no longer drops rows that miss only the response; it still drops rows with missing predictors, and na.action now applies to those.
  • size_shape() accepts a response with gaps, which it could not before: size is a mean of the traits and shape is a difference between them, so neither is defined for a row with a missing value. The response is completed first, by a maximum-likelihood multivariate normal estimated from the values that were measured (EM), and each gap becomes its conditional mean given the traits that individual has. The rest of the transformation is unchanged. $gaps reports how many entries were completed and $scores_sd the standard deviation of each completed score, which is 0 for the individuals that were measured in full. This is a point completion, so a fit on the resulting scores treats them as data: the spread in $scores_sd does not travel into that posterior. A row with nothing observed, and a pair of traits never measured together, are errors. pc1_variance_share(), plot_G_ellipses() and the diagnostic animal_design() runs on its response accept gaps for the same reason.
  • imputed_data() returns completed datasets, one per posterior draw: the observed entries as they are and the gaps filled on the response scale. An animal fit’s gaps are the parameters it sampled; a phenotypic fit has none, so its gaps are drawn from the normal conditional distribution given that row’s observed traits. print() reports each gap with its 95% interval. These are multiple imputations, not a single fill, and fit$draws("Y_mis") alone is not enough to reconstruct them: it is on the standardized scale and says nothing about which individual and trait each value belongs to.
  • lm_phen_cov() reports pointwise log_lik for the unstructured and factor fits, so loo and waic work for every model in the package. It is the density on the standardized response, as in the animal models.
  • Univariate fits report pointwise log_lik, so every model in the package now exposes the per-record terms that loo and waic need. The h2 and variance parametrizations describe the same model and report the same density.
  • fit_loo() compares fits by leave-one-out cross-validation, wrapping the loo package on the log_lik draws with the chain structure kept; criterion = "waic" gives WAIC, and loo(fit) dispatches to it once loo is loaded. The terms are the model block’s, one per record of the rotated response, so this compares model structures on the same data rather than leaving out one individual. loo is a new Suggests.
  • posterior_predictive() replicates the response from the posterior using the reported G, E or P, and reports the observed trait means, standard deviations and pairwise correlations against the replicates, with a tail probability for each (print()) and the distributions themselves (plot()). This is the individual-level check that fit_loo() is not.
  • breeding_values() predicts each individual’s additive genetic value, which the animal models integrate out and never report. It is the conditional mean (A %x% G) V^-1 (y - X beta) at the posterior means of G, E and beta, computed per individual through the eigendecomposition of A, and returns the predictions on the response scale with an optional standard error and the reliability 1 - Var(u | y) / diag(G). Being empirical Bayes, it does not propagate the uncertainty in the covariance parameters. Missing values are filled by their conditional mean first, which is exact for this linear predictor. Fits from lmm_animal() carry the data it needs; lm_phen_cov() and lmm_animal_gibbs() do not.

Changes

  • fit_draws(), draws_mean() and draws_quantile() now sign-align the factor loadings. A loading column is identified only up to its sign, so a chain can visit both orientations, and the average of the raw draws then cancels the factor out of a posterior mean or a heatmap. Each draw is flipped so that the trait with the largest mean absolute loading is positive, chosen once over the whole posterior. fit$draws("loadings") still returns the draws as the sampler wrote them; nothing else is reoriented, since column permutations and rotations are a different problem and are judged on G and communality.

Documentation

  • AGENTS.md states what each configuration reports, how the priors behave, and which quantities a factor model can and cannot identify.

stanimal 0.6.0

New features

  • lmm_animal() gains genetic_structure = "factor", which models the genetic covariance as a sparse factor structure on the correlation scale, G = diag(s_G) (Lambda Lambda' + Psi) diag(s_G), with regularized-horseshoe priors on the loadings (Piironen and Vehtari 2017). n_factors sets the number of factors; if it is omitted, the factor model starts from the sublinear default min(K - 1, max(2, floor(sqrt(K))), 20) and reports the value. hs_global_scale and hs_slab_scale control the shrinkage, and column_decay optionally multiplies the prior standard deviation of factor column m by column_decay^(m - 1) to favour decreasing factor magnitudes. The unstructured model remains the default. Factor fits report loadings, factor_magnitude, uniqueness, communality and s_G in addition to G, E, P, h2 and the other summaries.
  • lmm_animal() gains residual_structure = "shared_factor" for the shared-factor model G = Lambda diag(h2_factor) Lambda' + diag(psi_G) and E = Lambda diag(1 - h2_factor) Lambda' + diag(psi_E). The same latent factors structure both covariances, and the factor heritabilities identify how much of each factor is genetic; their beta prior is controlled by the existing beta_prior argument. It requires genetic_structure = "factor" and reports loadings, factor_magnitude, factor_heritability, genetic_uniqueness, residual_uniqueness, uniqueness and communality.
  • lm_phen_cov() gains covariance_structure = "factor", which replaces the unstructured phenotypic covariance with a sparse factor model on the correlation scale. It uses the same regularized-horseshoe loadings, n_factors default, hs_global_scale, hs_slab_scale and column_decay as the animal factor model, and reports loadings, factor_magnitude, uniqueness and communality. The factor fit estimates the residual standard deviations, so P, corrP and sigma_P describe the covariance left after the fixed effects rather than the marginal covariance of Y.
  • suggest_n_factors() chooses the number of factors from the data by parallel analysis (Horn 1965), comparing the eigenvalues of the residual trait correlation matrix against those of data with no shared structure. The result is an upper bound, and its attributes carry the full eigenvalue comparison. scree_eigenvalues() returns the eigenvalues behind a scree plot, and plot() draws it with the parallel-analysis cutoffs. Both residualize on the fixed effects first, so they describe the correlation the factor model fits.
  • The multivariate models now report pointwise log_lik, enabling LOO, WAIC and other predictive comparisons with the fits.
  • fit_draws() handles the factor outputs: factor fits return loadings as a trait by factor by draw array, uniqueness and communality as trait by draw matrices, and factor_heritability and factor_magnitude as factor by draw matrices.
  • Prior arguments are validated consistently even when the selected model does not use them, and explicitly supplying an unused prior now warns instead of being silently ignored.
  • examples/factor_model.R demonstrates the sparse factor model on a twelve-trait modular hierarchy, and examples/structure_comparison.R compares the unstructured, diagonal, factor and shared-factor covariance structures.

Bug fixes

  • Fits from the rstan backend now keep the trait and term names, so fit_draws() labels its arrays with the columns of Y and rename_beta() with the columns of X. Those attributes were only attached on the cmdstanr path, which left rstan fits with generic trait1, trait2 labels.
  • plot_prior_posterior() and plot_forest() compare against the prior the fit actually used instead of always drawing the unstructured one. lmm_animal() now records lkj_prior, beta_prior and parametrization on the fit, so an unstructured fit is compared with its own LKJ shape and a univariate parametrization = "h2" fit with its beta prior on the heritability (which animal_prior_draws() can now generate through beta_prior). A sparse factor fit has no closed-form prior to reproduce, so that combination errors and asks for an explicit prior rather than quietly plotting the wrong comparison.
  • The factor phenotypic model in lm_phen_cov() no longer pins the diagonal of P to the marginal variance of Y. Removing the fixed effects lowers the residual variance, so the model could only fit the likelihood by inflating the correlations. It now estimates a residual scale per trait, as the unstructured model does, and sigma_P is the residual standard deviation.

Changes

  • column_decay now defaults to 0.8 instead of 1 in both factor models. With no decay the factor columns are exchangeable a priori, so their labels are free to swap between chains and factor_magnitude reports large Rhat values on a healthy fit; the mild decay orders the columns without forcing a hierarchy. column_decay = 1 restores the previous behaviour. Supplying column_decay without a factor model now warns instead of erroring, like the other factor priors.
  • Leaving n_factors to the fallback now warns with the number it used, instead of reporting it with a message. The fallback only sees the number of traits; suggest_n_factors() is the data-driven answer.
  • Chains no longer all start at the same point. The sampler used to be called with init = 0; each chain now draws its own start from the engine default. A shared start makes chains agree by construction, so Rhat cannot detect a posterior mode that no chain visited. Pass init through ... to pin the start of a run that is hard to initialize.

stanimal 0.5.1

Name change

  • The package is now called stanimal instead of stanAnimal. The functions keep their names (lmm_animal(), animal_design(), makeA()), so only library(), the installed package name and the two cache settings change: options(stanAnimal.cache_dir = ) is now options(stanimal.cache_dir = ), and STANANIMAL_CACHE_DIR is now STANIMAL_CACHE_DIR. Compiled models are cached per package name, so the first fit after upgrading recompiles; stanimal_clear_cache() removes the old files.

New features

  • makeA() and animal_design() accept Gamma, a relationship matrix among founders, and groups, an optional founder-to-group assignment. This builds the A^Gamma relationship matrix for related founders and metafounders (Legarra et al. 2015): the founder block is initialized from Gamma instead of the identity, and the tabular recursion propagates those relationships. The default remains the standard pedigree with unrelated founders.
  • random_covariance() draws random covariance matrices for simulations, either from the LKJ distribution used as a prior by lmm_animal() (default), from the partial-correlation construction of evolqg::RandomMatrix(), or from a positive size factor mixed with a sign-oriented random LKJ residual (method = "factor"). The factor method solves the factor strength (or, for weak integration, a shrinkage toward independence) to match a requested integration level, keeps PC1 positive, and redraws the residual for every matrix, so draws at a fixed integration still differ. It spans the full range without the near-singular conditioning of bending an LKJ spectrum directly. The port handles one and two traits, where the original indexing fails, and both the LKJ and factor methods avoid the nearly singular matrices the partial method often produces. trait_comparison.R uses it for the simulated truth.
  • fit_draws() extracts the draws of a fit as arrays indexed by trait, with draws last and every dimension named: G, E, P, corrG, corrE, corrP are trait by trait by draw arrays and h2, sigma_G, sigma_E and sigma_P are trait by draw matrices, so posterior means and correlations no longer need a helper that matches G[i,j] variable names. It accepts the fits of lmm_animal(), lm_phen_cov() and lmm_animal_gibbs() (whose R is returned as E), posterior draws objects and back_transform() output, and derives quantities the fit does not report (P, corrE, corrP, sigma_G, sigma_E, sigma_P, h2).
  • draws_mean() and draws_quantile() summarise a fit or an fit_draws() object without the draw dimension, so draws_mean(fit, "G") is the posterior mean as a trait by trait matrix and draws_quantile(fit, "corrG") gives its interval. The examples and the README use them instead of defining their own post_mean() helper.
  • lmm_animal() and lm_phen_cov() keep the response column names on the cmdstanr fit, so fit_draws() and the summary functions label the trait dimensions without an extra argument.

Improvements

  • Declare the Stan project’s R-universe as an additional repository for cmdstanr and use it in the installation guidance.

  • Update package metadata and DOI references for the CRAN release.

  • lmm_animal_gibbs() validates its arguments with the same helpers as the Stan models instead of its own inline checks: Y and X through the shared response and design check, A through the shared symmetry and definiteness checks, and iter, warmup and thin through the shared iteration check. Its messages now name the argument the caller passed.

  • Input checks are uniform across the package: every error names its argument in backticks and is raised without a call, so the message points at Y, lkj_prior or maf rather than at the internal function that noticed. The checks live in utils.R and are reused, instead of each function testing its own conditions inline.

  • lmm_animal() and lm_phen_cov() check iter, warmup, chains, cores, cmd_stan and, for lmm_animal(), blend_A before fitting, so a warmup longer than the run is an error naming the argument instead of a failure inside the Stan call.

  • X is optional in lmm_animal(), lm_phen_cov() and lmm_animal_gibbs(). Leaving it out fits an intercept-only model: one column of ones named (Intercept), so the draws come out as beta[(Intercept)], as they do with an explicit intercept column, and beta keeps its trait dimension.
